feat: implement HTTP/2 rapid reset (CVE-2023-44487) protection

Add rate limiting protection against HTTP/2 rapid reset attacks by tracking
RST_STREAM frames in a sliding window (100 resets per 10 seconds). When the
threshold is exceeded, the server terminates the connection with a GOAWAY
frame using ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM error code.

Implementation:
- Track RST_STREAM frames in on_frame_recv_callback() and on_stream_close_callback()
- Sliding window counter resets after 10 seconds
- Connection terminated when >100 resets detected in window
- Comprehensive test suite verifies protection works without false positives

Testing:
- Normal requests: unaffected (5/5 pass)
- Rapid reset attack: connection terminated after ~100 resets (verified)

Also adds Python dependency management with uv via pyproject.toml for
improved test infrastructure.

feat: implement comprehensive timeout protection against slow HTTP attacks

Add per-stage timeout enforcement to prevent Slowloris, Slow POST, and Slow
Read attacks across all server implementations (HTTP/1.1, HTTPS, HTTP/2).

Changes:
- Created connection_timeouts.h with centralized timeout configuration
  - READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT_SEC (10s) - protects against Slowloris
  - READ_BODY_TIMEOUT_SEC (30s) - protects against Slow POST
  - WRITE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SEC (60s) - protects against Slow Read
  - SSL_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SEC (10s) - SSL handshake timeout
  - KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_SEC (5s) - keep-alive connection timeout
  - ConnectionState class for bandwidth tracking (MIN_DATA_RATE: 1KB/s)

- Updated AsioServer (HTTP/1.1):
  - Applied READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT to initial requests
  - Applied KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT to subsequent requests
  - Added write_response_with_timeout() with WRITE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT

- Updated AsioSSLServer (HTTPS):
  - Same timeout protections as AsioServer
  - SSL handshake timeout enforcement

- Updated Http2Server:
  - SSL handshake timeout in handle_connection()
  - Read timeout in main processing loop
  - Uses awaitable operators for timeout races

- Added test_slowloris.py test suite:
  - Slowloris attack detection
  - Slow Read attack detection
  - Legitimate client verification
  - Multiple slow connection resilience

Security Impact:
Prevents resource exhaustion via connection holdopen attacks. Server now
terminates slow connections after configured timeouts, maintaining
responsiveness to legitimate clients.

Testing:
Manual verification confirms connections terminate after 10s when headers
aren't completed. Legitimate requests remain unaffected.

Refs: ROADMAP.md Phase 2, Item #7

feat: implement argon2id password hashing to eliminate plaintext storage (CWE-256, CWE-916)

CRITICAL SECURITY FIXES:
- Replace plaintext password storage with argon2id hashing via libsodium
- Implement constant-time password comparison to prevent timing attacks
- Eliminate memory dump and config file password theft vulnerabilities

SECURITY IMPACT:
This commit addresses two CRITICAL vulnerabilities from the security roadmap:
1. CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of Password (CWE Top 25)
2. CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy (Timing Attack)

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS:

Password Hashing (auth.cc, auth.h):
- Add hash_password(): Uses crypto_pwhash_str with argon2id
  - OPSLIMIT_INTERACTIVE: 2 iterations (balance security/performance)
  - MEMLIMIT_INTERACTIVE: 64MB RAM (OWASP recommended)
  - Automatic unique salt per password (prevents rainbow tables)
  - PHC string format for hash storage

- Add verify_password(): Uses crypto_pwhash_str_verify
  - Constant-time comparison (prevents timing oracle attacks)
  - No information leakage via execution time

Authentication Updates:
- Update add_user() to hash passwords before storage
- Update validate_basic_auth() to use constant-time verification
- Digest auth marked deprecated (incompatible with hashed passwords)
- Digest auth fails gracefully for users with argon2id hashes

Backward Compatibility:
- load_users_from_file() supports both hashed and plaintext formats
- Auto-detect hash format ($argon2id$ prefix)
- Auto-hash plaintext passwords on load with warning
- Migration path for existing deployments

Build System:
- Add libsodium dependency to meson.build
- Update src/meson.build to link libsodium

Testing:
- Add test_password_security.py test suite
- Tests: Basic auth, hash format, timing attack resistance
- Manual testing confirms authentication working with hashed passwords

Documentation:
- Update ROADMAP.md to mark critical issues as FIXED
- Add security notes to code comments
- Recommend Basic+HTTPS over Digest auth

BREAKING CHANGES:
- Digest authentication incompatible with argon2id-hashed passwords
- Users should migrate to Basic authentication over HTTPS
- Password files with plaintext will show security warnings

OWASP/CWE Compliance:
- OWASP ASVS 2.4.1: Passwords stored using approved one-way hash
- OWASP ASVS 2.4.2: Salt of at least 32 bits (libsodium handles this)
- CWE-256: Unprotected Storage of Credentials - FIXED
- CWE-208: Observable Timing Discrepancy - FIXED
- CWE-327: Use of Broken Cryptographic Algorithm - PARTIALLY FIXED
  (MD5 still used for Digest auth protocol, but marked deprecated)

Tested-by: Manual testing with curl, Python test suite
Security-review: Implements OWASP password storage recommendations

fix: prevent HTTP request smuggling attacks (CWE-444)

Implemented comprehensive protection against HTTP request smuggling
vulnerabilities by adding validation for malicious header patterns:

Security Mitigations:
- Reject duplicate Content-Length headers
- Reject duplicate Transfer-Encoding headers
- Reject requests with both Content-Length AND Transfer-Encoding
- Validate Transfer-Encoding value is strictly "chunked"
- Normalize whitespace in Transfer-Encoding values

Attack Patterns Blocked:
- CL.TE (Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding) desync attacks
- TE.CL (Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length) desync attacks
- Duplicate header smuggling attempts
- Malformed Transfer-Encoding values (e.g., "chunked, identity")

Testing:
- Created comprehensive test suite (test_request_smuggling.py)
- All 9 security tests pass:
  - Duplicate Content-Length detection
  - Duplicate Transfer-Encoding detection
  - CL.TE smuggling prevention
  - TE.CL smuggling prevention
  - Malformed encoding rejection
  - Whitespace normalization
  - Invalid encoding rejection
  - Valid chunked request acceptance
  - Valid Content-Length request acceptance

This fix addresses ROADMAP Phase 1 issue #6 (HTTP Request Smuggling Risk).
Server now returns 400 Bad Request with descriptive error messages for
any smuggling attempts, preventing proxy/backend desynchronization.

feat: implement comprehensive request size limits to prevent DoS attacks

by sending giant headers, unlimited request bodies, or exploiting
HTTP/2 multiplexing with excessive streams.

feat: implement pre-fork worker pool for connection pooling

Add Apache-style pre-fork worker pool architecture to improve resource utilization and connection handling. Workers compete to accept connections using kernel-level locking, enabling efficient distribution of concurrent requests.

- Implement worker_loop() for persistent worker processes
- Add monitor_workers() to respawn workers after max requests
- Add cleanup_workers() for graceful shutdown
- Support configurable worker count via --workers option
- Add --max-requests-per-worker to prevent memory leaks
- Workers share listening socket for load balancing
- Maintain backward compatibility with traditional fork model

When --workers > 0, use pre-fork pool; otherwise use traditional fork-per-connection model for backward compatibility.
